- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model lags in correction; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% per day for 3–5 days post-shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 1.2x recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is flat (0.3–0.6) and price is rising, model often misses the peak; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for next 2–3 days.
